text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- EU Commissioner for humanitarian aid Emma Bonino will visit the flooded province of Opole, southwestern Poland, on Friday to make decisions on additional aid packages for the region's recovery.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The NBP has given a preliminary permit to Bank of America to start operations in Poland, the central bank said.
- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms operator, will give discounts on service fees to all victims of flooding whose telephone lines were cut off, the company said.
- The strategic investor in the Chelm cement mill, Atlas Neei Holdings Limited, has invested four million marks in the construction of an automated transport terminal.
The concern plans to invest up to 120 million marks in the plant's development to increase its output capacity.
- The Pafana tool maker in Pabianice, central Poland, has received an International Standards Organisation ISO-9001 quality product certificate, the plant said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's central bank will raise its basic credit interest rates in the next few weeks, National Bank of Poland (NBP) president Hanna Gronkiewicz Waltz said.

- Poland's three biggest distilleries, Polmos Poznan, Polmos Zielona Gora and Polmos Bialystok, might apply for a listing on the Warsaw bourse following a decision by the Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz in the next few weeks .
- A general shareholders meeting of the Ciech chemicals trader appointed Henryk Cuga new president on Tuesday.
The new board includes Ciech's former president Zdzislaw Matkiewicz, Krzysztof Staniszewski and Jan Zagajewski.

- Texaco oil group has purchased Amoco Poland Petroleum Products Limited including all Amoco's petrol stations operating in the country and plots of land under new petrol stations in construction. The two firms declined to disclose the value of the sale.
- The Szczecin shipyard made a net profit of 442,000 zlotys in the first half of 1997, the yard said.

- The ZEG SA electronic mining equipment maker in Tychy, southern Poland, plans an issue of up to 300,000 D-series shares to push up present share capital of 9.34 million zlotys by 25 percent, the firm said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Although 1997 direct foreign investment will be $1 billion lower than last year the economy's annual growth rate should remain at six percent, the cabinet's strategic studies centre (RCSS) said.
PARKIET

- The Universal trader plans soon to list in Warsaw three subsidiaries including Unimil contraceptive maker, the Trans Universal Poland forwarding firm and the Norblin steel products maker, Universal president Dariusz Przywieczerski said.
